title: Practice Set 1 — Kinematics MCQ Drill
notes:
Q1. A body starts from rest and moves with uniform acceleration a. Its velocity after time t is:
Answer: v = at

Q2. The slope of a velocity–time graph gives:
Answer: Acceleration

Q3. The area under a velocity–time graph gives:
Answer: Displacement

Q4. A ball is thrown vertically up with speed u. Its time of ascent is:
Answer: u/g

Q5. The horizontal range of a projectile is maximum when the angle of projection is:
Answer: 45°

Q6. At the highest point of its trajectory, the projectile has:
Answer: zero vertical velocity but non-zero horizontal velocity (u cosθ)

Q7. Two bodies of different masses are dropped from the same height in vacuum. They reach the ground:
Answer: simultaneously (same acceleration g)

Q8. For a body under uniform acceleration, distances in successive equal time intervals from rest are in the ratio:
Answer: 1 : 3 : 5 : 7 …

Q9. Relative velocity of two cars moving in the same direction with speeds 60 km/h and 40 km/h is:
Answer: 20 km/h

Q10. Maximum height of a projectile equals u² sin²θ/2g. For θ = 90° it becomes:
Answer: u²/2g (vertical throw)
confusion: A symbol is not a number until the unit is named.
A proportional relation is not an equality until the constant is included.
A vector answer needs a direction as well as a magnitude.
A special case, such as a right angle or a steady temperature, has to be stated before it is used.
keyPoints: Impulse = F Δt = change of momentum
tan of the angle of repose = μ
Quote the unit with the result.
importantStatements: Impulse is the area under a force-time graph and equals the change of momentum. A steady  force for a short time can change the momentum as much as a smaller force acting longer, if the products F Δt match. Action and reaction never cancel on one body, because they act on two bodies.
The working relations are Impulse = F Δt = change of momentum and tan of the angle of repose = μ. Name each symbol, convert the data into SI units, and only then substitute.
A 2.0 N force acts for 0.40 s on a 0.50 kg body that starts from rest. Find the impulse and the final speed. Impulse = F Δt = 2.0 × 0.40 = 0.80 N s. That equals the change in momentum.

exercises.question: A 2.0 N force acts for 0.40 s on a 0.50 kg body that starts from rest. Find the impulse and the final speed.
steps: That equals the change in momentum.
The reaction to this force acts on whatever applied the 2.0 N, not on the 0.50 kg body.

summary: Impulse equals change of momentum. A 2.0 N force for 0.40 s delivers 0.80 N s and takes a 0.50 kg body from rest to 1.6 m/s. The reaction is on the other body.
